PullRequest.Title: Align high contrast interaction states in the Agents window
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- Establish a shared interaction-state contract across Agents window controls, disclosures, popup lists, menus, split pickers, cards, and bespoke title-bar controls.
- Use dashed high-contrast boundaries for pointer hover while preserving solid keyboard-focus and persistent open/expanded/pressed states, selected palettes, and nested-action ownership.
- Add focused computed-style tests, Component Explorer fixtures, and reusable accessibility, theming, and fixture guidance.

## Issues addressed

| Severity | Issue | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| High | Hover could remove the keyboard focus ring from collapsible parent sessions. | Preserve the solid focus boundary on the painted inner tree row while allowing pointer-focused rows to remain dashed. |
| Medium | Menu and ActionList dead space or filter interaction could apply dashed styling to a stale focused row. | Enter pointer modality only for actionable rows and require the focused row to be actually hovered. |
| Medium | Nested Automation actions could highlight both the action and parent card. | Suppress the card boundary while its action group is hovered, focused, or open. |
| Medium | The Customizations header could render nested high-contrast outlines. | Assign the shared boundary to the header root and keep its pseudo-element fill-only. |
| Medium | Native disclosure summaries did not reflect their expanded state in HC. | Style `details[open] > summary` as a persistent solid state without adding redundant ARIA. |
| Medium | Expanded Get Started controls lost normal-theme hover feedback. | Keep hover fill independent from the HC persistent-state boundary. |

## Review status

- Unresolved actionable findings: None
- Residual risks: None

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate menus and action-list popups with mouse, touch, or keyboard in high-contrast themes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input handlers resolve the actionable row, switch a modality class, and update focus before the next paint. No external operation blocks interaction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pointer-move/key events and DOM ancestor depth; each event examines only the event target's shallow row ancestry, and action lists guard repeated modality updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser UI thread; events are processed serially with no queue, subprocess, IPC, or asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No data cache is involved. Existing focused-item identity avoids repeated item lookup/update within the same menu row; ActionListWidget also suppresses unchanged modality writes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed event handlers and modality setter implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style-recalculation cost varies by menu size and browser, but the changed work is constant and shallow per event, with unchanged focus-update cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds bounded target validation and modality state updates without multiplying focus/layout work or crossing an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover and keyboard-focus Agents window automation cards and shared interactive controls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS state matching occurs before paint; focusing one automation card creates one visible prompt hover and blur disposes it. No remote or persistent operation is on the path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct and position the prompt hover DOM/context view for the keyboard-focused card
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hover for the currently focused card; disposed on blur or card disposal
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing managed-hover show path also constructed and displayed a prompt hover on card focus; the diff changes ownership/targeting but not collection cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously when keyboard focus enters a card so the hover is visible immediately

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rendered automation cards and interaction transitions. Relational selectors inspect a card's direct action group, while hover construction is one per focused card rather than per collection item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI interaction at a time; no concurrent worker, IPC, network, filesystem, or database work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Automation card DOM and disposables are retained in the existing persistentCards map by automation ID and removed when automations disappear. The changed MutableDisposable replaces and disposes any prior focus hover.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from focus/blur handlers, HoverService creation flow, MutableDisposable replacement semantics, and persistent-card cleanup paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hover-widget implementation cost depends on content and viewport, but only one focused card is active and lifecycle cleanup is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: immediate hover work remains one-per-focus and is promptly disposed; CSS additions do not establish collection-wide relayout or retained growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and hover the active Sessions title-bar workspace and branch labels
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session state renders the title pill; after the normal hover delay, the content factory reads scrollWidth/clientWidth to decide whether a tooltip is needed. The read is off initial render and only affects tooltip display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read scrollWidth and clientWidth to determine text truncation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One geometry decision for the hovered workspace or branch label after hover delay
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hover content was always a static string, so no geometry read occurred and a hover widget was created even when text was fully visible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May require style/layout resolution before deciding whether to show the tooltip, but is not on startup or normal title rendering

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most two label elements (workspace and branch) per active pill and one geometry check per hover activation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single delayed hover timer on the UI thread; no parallel or queued external work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Managed-hover registrations live in _dynamicDisposables and are cleared whenever the pill rerenders. No result cache is needed because truncation can change with layout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from ManagedHoverWidget invoking the content factory only when the delayed hover is shown.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether layout is already clean at hover time varies, but cardinality is fixed and the new check avoids creating a tooltip for untruncated text.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the bounded delayed geometry check is limited to one label interaction and trades against avoiding unnecessary hover DOM construction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, recycle, scroll, and expand rows in the Sessions virtualized tree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each rendered session, section, or group row finds its owning .monaco-list-row and toggles a disclosure class before normal row rendering and paint.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible/recycled tree rows, not the full session history; one shallow closest traversal and one class toggle for each relevant row render.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Virtualized list rendering is synchronous on the UI thread and serialized; no new async work or boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The virtualized tree reuses row templates. toggle updates the reused row's disclosure state, preventing stale classes without retaining per-session state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the three renderer hunks and existing template-based list structure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible row count and rerender frequency vary with viewport and updates, but virtualization bounds the active DOM set and traversal depth is shallow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added work is constant per visible row and does not defeat virtualization, trigger geometry reads, or add collection-wide work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply shared hover, focus, selected, expanded, and nested-action styles across Agents window controls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser selector matching and paint occur when interaction classes/pseudo-classes change; the changes add outlines/background rules but no JavaScript work or external boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered controls affected by a state invalidation. Most selectors are scoped to agent-sessions workbench roots and direct component classes; :has selectors are limited to each automation card's direct action group.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style and paint pipeline on the UI thread; no application-level concurrency or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser style caches apply normally; no application cache or retained object collection is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the CSS-only hunks and scoped selectors.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific selector invalidation cost is not measured, but the selectors are scoped and interaction-driven rather than per-frame animation or global polling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: there is no concrete evidence of broad style invalidation, forced layout, unbounded DOM growth, or dropped-frame risk from the changed rules.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 63 changed-file patches and traced the runtime UI paths. The PR adds scoped interaction styling, bounded modality checks, one-per-hover overflow geometry decisions, and correctly disposed hover ownership. It introduces no external-boundary fan-out, unbounded retention, eager heavyweight initialization, or high-confidence synchronous UI regression.
